Real NYSED SEQ (Aug 2025 Set 1) — the relationship bullet, similarity/difference lane.
reps.prompt: Read and analyze the documents, then identify and explain a SIMILARITY or DIFFERENCE between the ideas in Documents 1 and 2. (Aug 2025 SEQ Set 1.)
reps.station_focus: Drill the similarity/difference move: state what changed or stayed the same across the two documents and explain its significance.

stimulus.content: Declaration of Independence excerpt on unalienable rights and government by consent.
stimulus.image_alt: Declaration of Independence excerpt on unalienable rights and government by consent.

reps.exemplar: Both founding documents rest on the same core idea — that government derives its authority from the people — but they differ in purpose, and that difference is significant. The Declaration of Independence (Doc 1) is a statement of principle justifying revolution: it asserts unalienable rights and the people's right to abolish a destructive government. The Preamble (Doc 2), written eleven years later, shifts from tearing down to building up: it lists the concrete goals of a functioning national government — union, justice, domestic tranquility, defense, welfare, and liberty. The continuity is popular sovereignty; the change is from justifying independence to establishing a durable framework to govern, showing how the founding generation moved from revolution to construction.
reps.compare_focus: Name whether it is a similarity or a difference, then explain WHY it matters — the significance is the move, not the observation.
